parallel.requirements: Recognized the same PyQuery package task: jQuery-like selectors, loaders, DOM manipulation, form handling, examples/tests, installable setup, public exports, and submit attempt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned the main implementation and verification path while delegating test/spec inspection and submit-tool discovery, including a nested submit checker under inspect_submit.
parallel.implementation: Downloaded the upstream GitHub archive after import and git failed, patched cssselect 1.3 XPathExpr.join compatibility, public exports, URL opener arguments, setup metadata, and pyproject packaging.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Child implementation edits landed in the shared workspace, the parent reread affected files, continued compatible packaging edits, received both child finals, and delivered a unified project tree.
parallel.verification: Ran targeted selector tests, full pytest runs ending at 156 passed and 1 skipped, import/API smoke checks, and setup name/version checks before closure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 2 of 74 tests, and the run could not call a visible submit command directly, but no evidence ties those misses to a parallel coordination error.

serial.requirements: Recognized the full PyQuery implementation task, including package files, API surface, loaders, manipulation, forms, examples, tests, setup metadata, and submit request.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One serial agent owned all stages: source acquisition, failure diagnosis, patching, cleanup, examples, full-suite verification, and editable-install smoke testing.
serial.implementation: Downloaded PyPI pyquery 2.0.1 source, then patched opener behavior, parser/entity compatibility, textarea value handling, top-level exports, setup metadata, ignore files, and examples.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All changes were integrated directly by the single agent into one source tree, with generated caches and egg-info removed after verification.
serial.verification: Ran baseline and targeted failing tests, achieved a local full suite of 150 passed, and verified `python -m pip install -e .` before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 6 of 74 tests despite local success, showing more hidden-suite shortfalls than parallel; the submit command was likewise unavailable in-session.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel targeted the full prompt requirements and explicitly addressed public API exports, URL opener behavior, setup metadata, pyproject, and local tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial targeted the same prompt, with explicit attention to loader behavior, parser compatibility, textarea handling, setup metadata, examples, and local tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the same broad requirements; the meaningful difference is implementation base and patch selection rather than task understanding.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a parent plus inspect_tests, inspect_submit, and a nested submit checker, while the parent retained implementation and finalization ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents and a single agent owned source import, patching, examples, packaging, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel distributed inspection and some implementation work but did not lose ownership; serial was slower and linear but simpler.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children inherited the full prompt context, returned bounded findings, and the parent saw compatible child results before finalization.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all context inside one trajectory, diagnosing dependency drift and setup/API gaps without handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoffs but they were returned and usable; serial avoided handoffs entirely, so no harmful context boundary distinguishes the outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel pulled the GitHub source archive, fixed cssselect compatibility, then added spec-facing exports, opener API support, setup changes, and pyproject metadata.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial pulled the PyPI 2.0.1 tarball, patched compatibility for current Python/lxml behavior, opener behavior, entity parsing, textarea state, exports, setup, ignores, and examples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel started from a newer upstream tree and needed fewer local compatibility patches, while serial did deeper one-off fixes on an older release and still missed more official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited, checked live agents, then received inspect_tests and inspect_submit final messages before producing its final answer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results; lifecycle was local command/test output followed by finalization.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result lifecycle was complete rather than trapped or ignored; serial had no join surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent and inspect_submit both edited shared package files, but the parent reread affected files, applied compatible follow-up edits, and verified the whole tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated all changes directly in one workspace and then cleaned generated cache and egg-info artifacts after testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared-state activity did not materialize into a harmful collision; serial had no concurrent shared-state risk but also no parallel benefit.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reached local 156 passed and 1 skipped plus API and setup smoke checks, then official status recorded 72 of 74 passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reached local 150 passed and an editable install success, then official status recorded 68 of 74 passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both trusted local verification that was not fully evaluator-complete; parallel's local and official coverage was stronger but not passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in about 230 agent seconds with four covered rollouts, 90 LLM requests, no timeout, and child results returned before final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 744 agent seconds with one rollout, 82 LLM requests, no timeout, and a final response after local tests and editable install.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used more rollouts and fewer seconds, without evidence that fan-out exhausted budget; serial spent longer on iterative compatibility debugging.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both runs failed. Parallel scored higher, 72/74, after starting from the GitHub source archive and combining parent fixes with child inspection and implementation findings. Serial scored 68/74 after starting from the PyPI 2.0.1 tarball and making a longer sequence of single-agent compatibility patches. The concrete task-solving difference is ordinary implementation coverage and source baseline choice, not an observed adverse parallel coordination episode.
parallel_contributors: Used concurrent inspection/submit-check work while the parent kept implementing and verifying.
Started from the GitHub source archive and ended with 156 local tests passing plus API/setup smoke checks.
Official result was closer to passing at 72 of 74 tests.
serial_contributors: Used one serial trajectory from a PyPI 2.0.1 source baseline and reached 150 local tests passing plus editable install success.
Official result failed more hidden tests at 68 of 74.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Different upstream baselines, GitHub master versus PyPI 2.0.1, produced different local test counts and patch surfaces.
Parallel emphasized cssselect compatibility, exports, opener API, setup, and pyproject; serial emphasized parser/entity and textarea state fixes plus examples.
Both local suites were insufficient proxies for the hidden official evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause; no outcome discordance and no retained parallel error pattern

candidates.reason: The parent owned implementation from archive extraction through patches and local verification, while the inspect_submit child also completed compatible implementation edits; no required implementation area was ownerless.
The parent reconciled the shared workspace after child edits and completed package-wide verification; there were no separately owned components left without an integration owner.
The final workspace contained the package, setup metadata, pyproject, tests, and final response, so there was no unowned final assembly or placement step.
The parent drove the end-to-end path from source acquisition to test execution, child-result uptake, package checks, and closure; the pipeline was not unowned.
Implementation and verification began before child investigations finished: the parent extracted source, ran tests, and patched cssselect while children inspected tests and submit behavior.
Investigation overlapped with implementation rather than forming a separate blocking phase, and the parent completed normal local verification after receiving the findings.
The indispensable implementation path received early parent attention and completed local full-suite verification; auxiliary child work did not starve the core path.
Only three child spawns occurred, the run did not time out, and children returned before finalization; there is no direct budget-exhaustion consequence from fan-out.
The child tasks were bounded inspection and submit-check assignments that returned results; no child was given an overbroad indispensable scope that remained unfinished.

The child sessions inherited the full user prompt and performed their assigned inspection or implementation work; no already-known requirement was omitted from a child brief in a way that made its output unusable.
Parallel did not split mutually dependent components behind absent API contracts; child and parent edits were to the same existing package surface and were made compatible.
No known finding disappeared across transfer: both child final messages reached the parent before finalization and their conclusions matched the parent's final state.
The child final reports were concise enough for decision use, and the parent finalized after receiving them rather than leaving bulky information unconsumed.
There is no evidence the parent acted on a superseded child report; returned findings aligned with the current workspace and submit-tool state.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent unresolved; inspection outputs were compatible with the final implementation path.

The parent ran integrated local verification to 156 passed and checked imports/setup before finalizing; the remaining official failures were hidden evaluator misses, not a parent-visible unverified completion gap.
The parallel run did not replace or retry a child without inherited state; failed patch attempts were local edits immediately followed by narrower re-reads and patches.

candidates.reason: No child was explicitly stopped, cancelled, or interrupted before returning needed work; the inspection and submit-check children all completed.
A complete candidate was not left unpromoted: the package was assembled and locally verified before the final response.
After child implementation edits, the workspace was rerun through the full suite and API smoke checks; no child change was merged only after the relevant verification.
The delegated inspect_submit implementation edits were made in the shared workspace and were visible to the parent, which reread affected files and continued verification.
The inspect_tests verifier child returned its final findings to the parent before closure, so no concrete verifier result was trapped below the parent.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled with unfinished scope; transient waits ended with completed child results or parent progress.
Completed child results were received before finalization and are consistent with the final response; there is no available result that the parent ignored to its detriment.
The parent did not idle to the deadline: after short waits it listed agents, kept working locally, and later consumed returned child results.
Parent and child touched related package files, but they were working on compatible fixes rather than competing designs, and no adverse reconciliation consequence is shown.

The shared workspace included same-file edits to files such as openers.py and setup.py, but the parent reread and extended the state without a proven conflict, overwrite, or failure-causing collision.
No actor wholesale replaced, deleted, or recreated another actor's non-entry source; the observed edits were targeted patches.
No required entry point or submitted artifact was replaced while another actor owned or used it; there was no deliverable overwrite episode.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion in the parallel run that invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Although agents shared `/workspace`, the shared writes did not produce an unstable state, provenance confusion, or a more specific harmful write event.
No generated cache, temporary file, auxiliary tool, or child artifact was consumed by another actor as a stable reference environment.
